args.text: [lane-plover] Three risks of caching DNS (Domain Name System, the internet's address book) answers for too long: (1) Stale addresses: if a site moves to a new server, users keep being sent to the old one and see errors or outages. (2) Slow recovery: when a fault is fixed or traffic is redirected, the change takes longer to reach everyone, which delays failover. (3) Lingering bad data: a forged or mistaken answer stays in the cache for longer, so harm from poisoning or misconfiguration lasts longer.

[lane-plover] Idempotent retries matter because networks fail in ways that leave you unsure whether a request worked, so you must be able to send it again. If repeating the request has the same effect as sending it once, a retry cannot cause double charges or duplicate records.

[lane-plover] Two trade-offs of UUIDv7 (Universally Unique Identifier, version 7) as a primary key: (1) it is time-ordered, so inserts stay fast and indexes stay compact, but the key leaks roughly when each row was created. (2) It takes 16 bytes, which is larger than a plain 4 or 8 byte integer, so indexes and foreign keys use more storage.

[lane-plover] A write-ahead log (WAL) records each change to durable storage before it is applied to the main data files. After a crash, the system replays the log to recover committed changes and discard unfinished ones, so no data is lost or left half-written.

[lane-plover] Two reasons to pin a client version in a benchmark: (1) results stay comparable between runs, because a client update could change speed and hide or fake a real difference. (2) Runs are reproducible, so others can repeat the test and get the same setup.
